rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: tenant selection and source-of-income protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Any tenant-selection standard must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants, such as ability to pay rent and to care for the apartment.
rules.key_value: No source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8); uniform reasonable standards
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.penalty: Civil fines up to $300 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages and other remedies after hearing.

rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords must give tenants the city's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and whenever legal steps to end a tenancy (e.g., Notice to Quit or Summary Process) are taken. The ordinance does not bar evictions otherwise allowed by law.
rules.key_value: Guide required at tenancy start and at termination; $300 per day fine
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process)
rules.effective_date_note: Only the page posting date (10/14/2020) is given; actual ordinance effective date not stated.
rules.exemptions: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, or in a non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility; short-term rental units under Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, § 4.60. Applies to owner-occupied single units.
rules.penalty: Fine of $300 for each day's violation (Sec. 8.71.070).

unverifiable_exemptions: hospital, skilled nursing or health facility units
non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities

rules.review_note: Notification requirement only; does not restrict grounds for eviction.

no_rule_findings.finding: Cambridge has only passed a policy order directing the city manager to draft options or ordinance language on banning algorithmic rent-pricing software; no ban is in force.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The policy order directs the city manager work with relevant city departments to draft policy options or ordinance language that will be presented back to council later this term
no_rule_findings.basis_citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (Sobrinho-Wheeler), algorithmic rent pricing

dropped_candidates.reason: Policy order, not a rule; kept as a no_rule_finding for algorithmic_rent_setting.

parsed.notes: Cambridge has no local rent control (state bar, G.L. c. 40P, applies) and the documents provided don't cover deposits, application fees or rent caps for the city.
